title: Shaft Sleeve
model_title: Pump Shaft Sleeve (Hook-Type) under the Packing, with Impeller Hub & Nut

introduction.definition: A shaft sleeve is a replaceable tube over the pump shaft where packing or a seal runs. It protects the shaft from wear and corrosion; when grooved it is replaced instead of the shaft. It is keyed or clamped to turn with the shaft, located against the impeller hub and sealed with an O-ring.
applications: Packed and mechanically sealed centrifugal pumps
introduction.summary: A shaft sleeve is a replaceable, hard-wearing tube fitted over the pump shaft where packing or seals run, so the sleeve wears instead of the shaft.

wear.title: The sleeve wears, not the shaft
wear.description: Packing (and some seal elastomers) rub on the shaft surface and slowly cut a groove, worst under the rings nearest the gland. A replaceable, hard-coated sleeve takes this wear and protects the expensive shaft from wear and corrosion; it is renewed at overhaul. The sleeve is keyed or clamped to turn with the shaft, located against the impeller hub, and sealed with an O-ring so liquid cannot creep along the shaft underneath. Check sleeve runout (≈ ≤ 0.05 mm TIR typical) after fitting.

video_tutorials.title: Shaft Sleeve — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Shaft Sleeve.
Monitor packing leakage (sleeve wear sign).
Inspect sleeve at repack.
Replace sleeve and O-ring.
Watch for grooving: packing cannot be adjusted. Common cause: abrasives, over-tightened packing.
Watch for leak under sleeve: leak despite good packing. Common cause: o-ring missing / damaged.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
